First, let's factor $p$ from the expression. We have

$$
9p+p{t}^{2}=p(9+{t}^{2}).
$$

Let's now focus on factoring the expression $(9+{t}^{2}).$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}9+{t}^{2} & =9-(-{t}^{2}) \\  & =9-({\text{i}}^{2}{t}^{2}) \\  & ={3}^{2}-(\text{i}t)^{2} \\  & =(3+\text{i}t)(3-\text{i}t)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
p(9+{t}^{2})=p(3+\text{i}t)(3-\text{i}t).
$$
